subject: Request: Temporary latency tolerance for PilotHQ preview launch
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pilothq.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Temporary latency tolerance for PilotHQ preview launch

Hi Jordan —

Great talking yesterday; excited PilotHQ is ready to kick off the 3-week preview next Tuesday. A quick operational ask from our side before we hand over the preview link: PilotHQ’s preview workload has a heavier-than-expected long-tail on sequence length (few very large prompts), and our initial sims show periodic 95th/99th percentile latency spikes during the first week as caches warm and routing settles.

We want to be transparent: we’re asking for a temporary, narrowly-scoped latency tolerance for the preview period rather than the standard 99.9% 200ms target in our production SLA. Specifically:
- Duration: 3 weeks (preview window)
- Scope: up to 5% of requests can exceed the standard latency guardrail, primarily at the 95th/99th percentile and only during cache-warmup and model-rollout windows
- Mitigations: prefix caching, bumping burst capacity, and a canary rollout that we’ll run overnight the first two days

Can you confirm PilotHQ is comfortable with a limited operational tolerance during the preview, and whether contracts@pilothq.com needs a redline to the SLO language? If helpful I’ll loop in Marissa and Logan (runtime/ops) to share the short mitigation plan and a lightweight runbook.

Thanks — want to make the preview low-friction but honest about the tradeoffs so we don’t surprise your engineering team.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0137

Attachment stubs: pilot-preview-slo-redline.pdf (proposed language), pilot-preview-runbook-diff.txt (ops changes)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pilothq.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary latency tolerance for PilotHQ preview launch

Rishi —

Appreciate the heads-up and the specificity. PilotHQ is generally open to a short preview tolerance as long as it’s documented and we retain the option to pause the preview if customer-facing SLAs are materially impacted. A couple quick questions from our side:
1) Does the 5% allowance apply globally across all endpoints, or just the long-tail embed/generation endpoints?
2) Can you provide a short, non-technical summary I can share with our Ops and Legal?
3) Would Redwood be willing to commit to a post-preview remediation plan (e.g., concrete quant improvements and timeline) if we observe unacceptable degradation?

Contracts should look at any redline; I’ve CC’d contracts@pilothq.com in case they want an early peek. If you can send the redline and the runbook diff we’ll review first thing Monday.

— Jordan
Jordan Lee | Head of Platform Integrations
PilotHQ
jordan.lee@pilothq.com

Note: we prefer not to have public-facing users on the preview. Internal-only for 3 weeks.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pilothq.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary latency tolerance for PilotHQ preview launch

Jordan, Rishi —

Thanks — quick operational note from the runtime/ops side. Answering Jordan’s questions:
- The 5% allowance is scoped to the generation endpoints (text + chat) and specifically to requests with sequence lengths > 2k tokens. Embeddings are excluded unless you run long-context embedder jobs.
- Non-technical summary for your ops/legal: for a 3-week preview we will accept that a small fraction (<=5%) of very large requests may hit elevated latency while our caches and routing learn the workload pattern. We will monitor and provide daily reports; PilotHQ retains the right to pause the preview if SLA breaches affect customer-facing traffic.
- Post-preview remediation: if we observe recurrent breaches above the tolerance window, Redwood will prioritize (a) quantization/engine tuning, (b) targeted autoscale policy adjustments for your workspace, and (c) a follow-up 2-week stabilization window with no charge for extra capacity used during remediation. Specific remediation milestones will be documented in the preview closeout note.

Attachments: I’m attaching two short files — the proposed redline to the SLO paragraph (pilot-preview-slo-redline.pdf) and an ops diff that lists the runbook changes we’ll make (pilot-preview-runbook-diff.txt).

Operational safeguards we’ll apply the first 48 hours:
- Canary ramp: start with 5% of traffic for the first 4 hours and observe token-level latency; 25% for next 20 hours; full preview only after green on canary.
- Auto-fallback: route to lower-latency quantized variant automatically if 95th percentile climbs beyond the temporary boundary for 30 minutes.
- Daily dashboard: push a short daily digest to your channel with 95/99p metrics and any cache-miss spikes.

If that all sounds acceptable we can proceed; Jordan, if legal wants any alternate wording we can iterate quickly.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Director, Runtime Ops
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pilothq.com>, contracts@pilothq.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Bcc:
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary latency tolerance for PilotHQ preview launch

Jordan / Contracts team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Marissa’s notes, Redwood can proceed with the temporary, scoped tolerance limited to generation requests >2k tokens for the 3-week preview. Key points agreed:
- Tolerance window: up to 5% of qualifying requests may exceed standard latency SLOs during the preview window (3 weeks).
- Scope & safeguards: canary ramp, automatic fallback to quantized variant, daily reporting, and PilotHQ right to pause.
- Remediation: if tolerances are repeatedly exceeded, Redwood will trigger the remediation plan (engine tuning + stabilization window) and cover extra capacity charges during the remediation period.

Attached are the two files Marissa mentioned — pilot-preview-slo-redline.pdf and the ops diff. Please confirm acceptance by EOD Tuesday so we can start the canary on Wednesday morning PST. If contracts want wording changes we can accept a one-paragraph amendment in the Master Services Agreement for the preview (example language in the attached PDF).

I’ll schedule a short 20-minute call Wednesday 07:30-07:50 PST to walk through the canary plan if useful.

Best —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0137

Attachments: pilot-preview-slo-redline.pdf (1 page redline), pilot-preview-runbook-diff.txt (ops checklist)
